# lumen_cc_pair (Resource)

A connector-credential pair: the object that actually indexes. It joins an `lumen_connector` to an `lumen_credential` and carries the access control for the documents they produce.

Creating a pair starts indexing. Destroying one removes the indexed documents too, which runs in the background — Terraform waits for it to finish.

~> **Drift blind spot.** Lumen does not report `groups`, `auto_sync_options` or `processing_mode` back on read, so Terraform cannot detect changes made to them elsewhere. They are recorded from the configuration at create time. After `terraform import` they are empty, and setting them then replaces the pair.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A connector-credential pair is the object that actually indexes. It joins a
# connector to the credential it authenticates with, and carries the access
# control for the documents they produce.
resource "lumen_cc_pair" "confluence_wiki" {
  name          = "confluence-wiki"
  connector_id  = lumen_connector.confluence.id
  credential_id = lumen_credential.confluence.id

  # Everyone can read the indexed documents. Use "private" with groups to
  # restrict them, or "sync" to mirror permissions from the source system.
  access_type = "public"
}

# A pair whose documents only two groups may read.
resource "lumen_cc_pair" "hr_handbook" {
  name          = "hr-handbook"
  connector_id  = lumen_connector.hr_drive.id
  credential_id = lumen_credential.hr_drive.id

  # This side owns the link, so a group never fights the pair over it.
  access_type = "private"
  groups      = [lumen_user_group.hr.id, lumen_user_group.legal.id]

  # Pause a pair to stop new index runs. It keeps the documents it has.
  paused = false
}

# Destroying a pair also removes the documents it indexed, which Lumen does in
# the background. Raise the timeout for a connector holding many documents.
resource "lumen_cc_pair" "large_archive" {
  name          = "large-archive"
  connector_id  = lumen_connector.archive.id
  credential_id = lumen_credential.archive.id

  timeouts {
    delete = "2h"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connector_id` (String) Id of the connector to pair, e.g. `lumen_connector.docs.id`.
- `credential_id` (String) Id of the credential to pair, e.g. `lumen_credential.docs.id`.
- `name` (String) Pair name, shown in the admin panel. Lumen does not require it to be unique, but a connector and credential can only be paired once.

### Optional

- `access_type` (String) Who may read the indexed documents: `public` (everyone), `private` (the groups below), or `sync` (mirrored from the source system). `sync` needs a Business tier license and a source that supports permission sync.
- `auto_sync_options` (String) Permission-sync settings as a JSON object. Only meaningful with `access_type = "sync"`.
- `groups` (Set of Number) User group ids that may read the documents. Applies when `access_type = "private"`.
- `paused` (Boolean) Pause indexing. A paused pair keeps its documents but runs no new index attempts.
- `processing_mode` (String) How fetched documents are processed. Defaults to `REGULAR`, the full index pipeline. `RAW_BINARY` stores the file without extracting text. `FILE_SYSTEM` is deprecated and produces documents that cannot be searched.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric connector-credential pair id.
- `last_index_attempt_status` (String) Status of the most recent index attempt, or null before the first one runs.
- `num_docs_indexed` (Number) Documents currently indexed by this pair.
- `status` (String) Server status: `SCHEDULED`, `INITIAL_INDEXING`, `ACTIVE`, `PAUSED`, `DELETING` or `INVALID`. Lumen cycles it as indexing progresses; use `paused` to change it.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/sh
# Import by numeric connector-credential pair id.
#
# Lumen does not report groups, auto_sync_options or processing_mode, so they
# are empty after an import. Setting them afterwards replaces the pair.
terraform import lumen_cc_pair.confluence_wiki 12
```
